content.storyline: Houston enters this AFC South matchup after losing 27-24 to Cleveland despite leading 17-3, with its playoff hopes still in play. Indianapolis beat Houston 19-17 in Week 3 and comes in after a 24-22 win over Miami.

In Week 10, Indianapolis beat Miami 24-22, while Houston lost to Cleveland 27-24.
Indianapolis won the teams’ Week 3 meeting, 19-17.
Houston had 33 defensive sacks, second in the league; Indianapolis had 22, ranking 14th.

excerpts: Thursday night’s divisional tussle had the potential to mark the Texans’ return to .500, with Houston riding the wave to a potential second-half surge. Instead, after blowing a 17-point lead to the Browns [on Sunday](https://www.nfl.com/games/texans-at-browns-2026-reg-10?tab=recap) , Houston heads home licking its wounds and hoping to launch one last-ditch effort to rescue its season from massive disappointment. Standing in the Texans’ way are the rival Colts, who [narrowly defeated](https://www.nfl.com/games/dolphins-at-colts-2026-reg-10?tab=recap) the rebuilding Dolphins last week but have lost 14 of their last 17 games dating back to the 2025 season. They beat Houston, 19-17, [in Week 3](https://www.nfl.com/games/texans-at-colts-2026-reg-3?tab=recap) , but that was before Indianapolis held [its fire sale](https://www.nfl.com/news/nfl-trade-deadline-track-every-move-since-start-of-2026-regular-season) leading up to the trade deadline. So, will both AFC South squads be commiserating over a lost season when the clock hits zeros on Thursday, or will the Texans emerge clinging to at least a sliver of hope heading into Thanksgiving?

Offensive coordinator Nick Caley faced questions -- including from Texans [starting guard Ed Ingram](https://x.com/Cody_Stoots/status/2122375825529913697) \-- about his ability to make in-game adjustments after the offense went three-and-out on six of its last eight possessions against Cleveland last week, turning what was once a 17-3 lead into a 27-24 loss. They have now lost four games in which they held a fourth-quarter lead (most in the NFL), blowing a lead in the final two minutes of regulation four times. They are the 14th team since 1982 with four or more such losses in a season. Of that group, only the 2022 Ravens made the playoffs (Baltimore lost in the opening round). The Texans are four games behind the Jaguars in the AFC South race and 2.5 games behind the Browns for the final AFC wild-card spot. Plus, Cleveland holds the head-to-head tiebreaker after upsetting Houston on Sunday. Yes, things look bleak, but DeMeco Ryans’ crew isn’t dead yet. While the Colts’ playoff probability will be less than 5% whether they win or lose on Thursday, the Texans’ chances are currently at 20% and they have the league’s fourth-easiest remaining strength of schedule. A Week 11 loss would drop Houston’s odds to 7%, per Next Gen Stats.
